# Neural Radiance Fields

Also called: Explicit Radiance Field Representations, Implicit Radiance Field

## Overview
Neural Radiance Fields ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) represent a static 3D scene as a continuous volumetric function that maps a 3D spatial position and a 2D viewing direction to an emitted RGB color and a volume density scalar [S1][S3]. It solves the problem of novel view synthesis by replacing explicit geometric primitives (meshes or point clouds) with an implicit neural representation encoded in the weights of a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) [S1]. Unlike its siblings, NeRF explicitly models view-dependent appearance by conditioning the color output on the viewing direction, while keeping the density view-independent [S1]. It distinguishes itself from [explicit radiance field](#806-explicit-radiance-fields.md) alternatives by maintaining a continuous spatial representation, albeit at higher computational cost [S1].

## Shared principles
The family relies on the differentiability of the forward rendering operator and the propagation of gradients through the integration steps [G]. The core mechanism is the evaluation of the [volume rendering equation](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md) and the computation of gradients with respect to scene parameters (density, geometry, transfer functions, camera poses) [G].

The standard [emission-absorption model](#927-emission-absorption-model.md) computes the color $\hat{C}(\mathbf{r})$ for a ray $\mathbf{r}$ as:

$$
\hat{C}(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^N T_i (1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)) \mathbf{c}_i
$$

where $\sigma_i$ is the density, $\delta_i$ is the step size, $\mathbf{c}_i$ is the color, and $T_i = \exp\left(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j\right)$ is the transmittance [G].

Differentiation strategies fall into three main categories [G]:
1. **Reverse-Mode [Automatic Differentiation](#7151-automatic-differentiation-reverse-adjoint-mode.md) (AD):** Standard backpropagation through the computational graph.
2. **[Adjoint Method](#789-adjoint-method.md):** Computes gradients by propagating adjoint variables backward through the rendering algorithm.
3. **Analytic Inversion / [Explicit Gradients](#7613-analytical-gradients.md):** Uses a-priori knowledge of the DVR operations to derive closed-form gradients, reducing memory consumption.

## Subtopics

### [NeRF (Neural Radiance Fields)](1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)
NeRF represents a static 3D scene as a continuous volumetric function mapping 3D position and 2D viewing direction to RGB color and volume density. It solves novel view synthesis by replacing explicit geometry with an [implicit MLP](#14283-shallow-mlp-decoder.md). Sets itself apart by explicitly modeling view-dependent appearance via direction conditioning while keeping density view-independent. Choose for high-quality static scene reconstruction.

### [Neural Reconstruction in the Wild](6202-neural-reconstruction-in-the-wild.md)
A NeRF method for large-scale, real-world scenes. Addresses low geometric quality and coarse details in expansive environments using surface-guided sampling. Choose when reconstructing large outdoor scenes.

### [Point-NeRF](6569-point-nerf.md)
A [point-based NeRF representation](#15538-point-nerf-representation.md) synthesizing novel views by aggregating features from a sparse 3D [neural point](#7266-neural-points.md) cloud. Differs from [grid-based NeRF](#13738-voxel-and-sparse-grid-representations.md) by replacing dense volumetric grids with learnable points, enabling faster training. Choose for efficient surface-restricted rendering.

### [Volume Feature Rendering](6628-volume-feature-rendering.md)
A [differentiable rendering](#16276-differentiable-rendering.md) technique integrating queried feature vectors along a ray into a single aggregated vector, transformed to pixel color by one network evaluation. Reduces computational cost compared to standard volume rendering. Choose when minimizing neural network evaluations is critical.

### [Neural Rendering](6800-neural-rendering.md)
Learns the rendering process directly from data rather than handcrafted analytical differentiation. Jointly trains a scene generation and rendering network. Choose when bypassing explicit geometric differentiation is preferred.

### [Fourier Features Mapping](8242-fourier-features-mapping.md)
A preprocessing technique transforming low-dimensional coordinates into a higher-dimensional space using sinusoidal functions to overcome MLP spectral bias. Decouples neural architecture from spatial representation. Choose to accelerate high-frequency detail learning.

### [Reflection-aware NeRF](8310-reflection-aware-nerf.md)
Jointly models planar surfaces and explicitly casts reflected rays to capture high-frequency reflections. Prevents false geometry duplication along primary rays. Choose for scenes with strong planar reflections.

### [GRAF](8539-graf.md)
A generative model for 3D-aware image synthesis learning a conditional radiance field from unposed 2D images via [adversarial training](#14030-adversarial-training-gan.md). Allows explicit control over camera pose, shape, and appearance. Choose for 3D-aware generation from unposed images.

### [Flash Cache](9550-flash-cache.md)
A volumetric inverse rendering method reducing bias and variance in radiance estimation by using a high-capacity NeRF as a control variate for incoming illumination. Choose for unbiased radiance estimation in complex lighting.

### [C-ToF Gaussian Splatting](9678-c-tof-gaussian-splatting.md)
Not given in the sources.

### [Generative Neural Feature Fields (GIRAFFE)](10047-generative-neural-feature-fields-giraffe.md)
Models individual objects using separate, compositional [neural feature fields](#10047-generative-neural-feature-fields-giraffe.md) for disentangled pose, shape, and appearance control. Assigns each object its own MLP outputting density and feature vectors. Choose for compositional scene generation.

### [NeRDF Learning via Knowledge Distillation](10226-nerdf-learning-via-knowledge-distillation.md)
Accelerates NeRDF optimization by using a pre-trained teacher NeRF to generate pseudo-training views. Avoids spatial high-frequency artifacts from sparse inputs. Choose for fast training of duplex radiance fields.

### [Fourier Feature Encoding](10580-fourier-feature-encoding.md)
Maps scene coordinates and viewing directions to high-dimensional sinusoidal features to address spectral bias. Uses fixed, non-trainable bases. Choose for standard [positional encoding](#876-positional-encoding.md) in coordinate-based networks.

### [Voxel-based Representation](10852-voxel-based-representation.md)
Replaces continuous MLP queries with discrete 3D grids storing volumetric features, density, or color. Enables hardware-accelerated lookups. Choose for memory efficiency and inference speed.

### [Neural Volume Super-Resolution](11444-neural-volume-super-resolution.md)
Super-resolves volumetric [neural scene representations](#12421-implicit-methods-sdf-based.md) directly in 3D to generate geometrically consistent high-resolution views. Guarantees consistency across viewing directions. Choose for 3D-consistent upscaling.

### [Volumetric Supervision for NeRF](11452-volumetric-supervision-for-nerf.md)
Improves canonical volume fidelity in [dynamic tomography](#7376-dynamic-tomographic-reconstruction-with-motion-identificatio.md) by combining projection training with [volumetric supervision](#11100-volumetric-supervision.md) from high-fidelity X-CT data. Choose when external 3D scans are available for supervision.

### [NeRF-MAE](11769-nerf-mae.md)
A self-supervised pretraining framework masking and reconstructing patches from an explicit radiance/density grid. Enables large-scale unlabeled data usage. Choose for self-supervised 3D representation learning.

### [Distilled Feature Fields](12026-distilled-feature-fields.md)
Extends NeRF with a 3D neural [feature field](#12995-feature-fields.md) mapping coordinates to semantic descriptors, enabling query-based local editing. Choose for open-set semantic [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) and editing.

### [NeuralRadianceFieldPackedRenderer](13115-neuralradiancefieldpackedrenderer.md)
A differentiable rendering component for pipelines combining NeRF with PackedRFTracer. Orchestrates neural field evaluation along traced rays. Choose as a default fallback renderer for PackedRFTracer backends.

### [Semi-Gradient Method](13620-semi-gradient-method.md)
Modifies the baseline loss by applying a stop-gradient to the RHS of the rendering equation to remove gradient bias and high variance. Choose for stable optimization of radiance field caching.

### [Hybrid Surface-Volume and Mesh Representation](13663-hybrid-surface-volume-and-mesh-representation.md)
Integrates explicit geometric primitives or implicit surface fields with neural radiance fields to decouple geometry from appearance. Choose for faster convergence and unambiguous geometry.

### [Dynamic and Deformation Modeling](13664-dynamic-and-deformation-modeling.md)
Extends static NeRFs to reconstruct time-varying scenes by incorporating temporal information or warping to canonical space. Choose for non-static content reconstruction.

### [Reference-Based Non-Photorealistic Radiance Fields](15643-reference-based-non-photorealistic-radiance-fields.md)
Transfers style from a 2D reference image to a 3D radiance field using explicit and implicit supervision. Choose for controllable 3D stylization.

### [Conditional Radiance Field Architecture](15951-conditional-radiance-field-architecture.md)
Conditions the volumetric representation on instance-specific latent codes to model entire object classes. Disentangles shape and appearance. Choose for class-level generation and editing.

### [StyleRF](17768-stylerf.md)
A zero-shot 3D style transfer technique performing style transformation within the feature space. Choose for arbitrary new style generalization.

### [UV Volumes Framework](18037-uv-volumes-framework.md)
Encodes low-frequency semantic information in 3D [UV volumes](#18151-uv-volumes.md) and high-frequency appearance in a 2D [neural texture](#16067-neural-textures.md) stack. Choose for real-time free-view video synthesis with pose/shape editing.

### [Hierarchical and Distributed Optimization](18222-hierarchical-and-distributed-optimization.md)
Scales NeRF training to large scenes or corrects imperfect poses by decomposing the optimization problem. Choose for large-scale scenes or pose correction.

### Hierarchical Geometric Guidance
A [volume sampling](#7111-volume-sampling.md) strategy incorporating sparse depth priors from [Structure from Motion](#16341-structure-from-motion-sfm.md) (SfM) into scene representations by sampling volume points in a local-to-global manner [S4, unofficial]. It initializes sampling around the depth prior in a local region and gradually extends to full scene bounds, mitigating geometric misalignment caused by depth prior bias [S4, unofficial].

### Pose-Related Shading Factor
Decomposes radiance color into pose-independent RGB color $c_0$ and pose-dependent shading factor $s$ to handle bent rays and self-occlusion in posed humans [S5, unofficial]. The shared color and feature vector are predicted by an appearance network, while a shallow shading network estimates $s$ conditioned on the target pose $\theta_t$, yielding $c = c_0 s$ [S5, unofficial].

### Density Field Prediction
An MLP $F_\sigma$ that predicts density $\sigma$ using an interpolated geometry latent code $l_{geo}$ and signed height indicator $\tilde{h}$ [S5, unofficial]. The density is computed as $\sigma = F_\sigma(\phi(\tilde{h}), l_{geo})$, where $\phi(\cdot)$ is the position encoding function [S5, unofficial].

### Neural Appearance Blending
A neural blending scheme for appearance refinement that recovers texture information from two adjacent input views to address artifacts from sparse inputs [S6]. It back-projects points from a target view depth map into neighboring views, extracts features and visibility, and feeds them into a blending network to compute weights $W_q = \mathbf{MLP}_\mathcal{A}(f^{\mathbf{v}_1}_q, O^{\mathbf{v}_1}_q, f^{\mathbf{v}_2}_q, O^{\mathbf{v}_2}_q)$, yielding $C^{v*}_q = W_q \cdot C_q$ [S6].

### Two-layer Volumetric Rendering
Splits the model into two layers with separate density and appearance modules for the object and environment to allow foreground extraction and support effects like translucency [S7, unofficial]. Sample points inside a 3D bounding box use the foreground layer, outside use the background layer [S7, unofficial]. Total density is $\sigma_i = \sigma_{io} + \sigma_{ie}$, and color is $c_i = (\sigma_{io} c_{oi} + \sigma_{ie} c_{ei}) / \max(\sigma_i, \epsilon)$ [S7, unofficial].

### Grid-guided Neural Radiance Field
A mechanism where the [NeRF branch](#17510-grid-guided-nerf-branch-training.md) provides global regularization and pointwise guidance to refine independently optimized grid features, addressing noisy artifacts and lack of space continuity in grid-based methods [S8]. The grid branch enriches scene information via reconstruction loss while the NeRF branch focuses on missing high-frequency details, allowing joint refinement rather than freezing grids [S8].

### Multi-view Distillation Optimization
An optimization strategy using [multi-view distillation](#10226-nerdf-learning-via-knowledge-distillation.md) information to guide training of the [NDRF](#18147-neural-duplex-radiance-fields-ndrf.md), suppressing artifacts and approximating original [NeRF rendering](#5124-nerf-rendering-alpha-compositing.md) quality [S9]. It renders views from distillation cameras using the original NeRF to obtain targets, renders from training cameras using NDRF, and optimizes via render loss [S9].
